mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month predicts a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days due to weakening consumer demand and construction sector underperformance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below the median baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which is associated with lower earnings growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods or the average return is not below the 5th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% combined with a federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which historically precedes equity market corrections and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals robust labor market expansion, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes or the median return is below the 50th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 10% for two consecutive months, alongside a decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which historically precedes equity market weakness as consumers delay discretionary purchases.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS m/m > 10% for 2 consecutive months AND GDPC1 m/m < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes or the average return is not below the 25th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000,000 units for three consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, is associated with a contraction in the housing sector and reduced construction-related economic activity, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to rapid negative earnings revisions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods or the median return is not below the 40th percentile of historical 5-day returns.
